views.name: cleaned_weekly_sales_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  CAST(transactions AS INTEGER) AS transactions,
  CAST(sales AS INTEGER) AS sales,
  CAST(week_number AS INTEGER) AS week_number,
  CAST(month_number AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
  CAST(calendar_year AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
  age_band AS age_band,
  demographic AS demographic,
  CAST(avg_transaction AS REAL) AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
WHERE week_date_formatted IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical projection of cleaned_weekly_sales that ensures consistent date and numeric types, preserves demographic attributes and measures. Use this to join to other tables or aggregate by calendar_year/week_number/month_number or demographics. | Use for: time series of sales/transactions by region/platform/segment/customer_type; demographic breakdowns of average transaction or sales; aggregations by calendar_year/month_number/week_number

views.name: weekly_sales_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  CAST(transactions AS INTEGER) AS transactions,
  CAST(sales AS INTEGER) AS sales
FROM weekly_sales
WHERE week_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical projection of weekly_sales with typed measures and preserved categorical columns. Use for simple weekly-level aggregations or to union with other weekly facts. | Use for: compare weekly_sales to cleaned_weekly_sales; aggregate transactions or sales by region/platform/segment/customer_type

views.name: veg_txn_lines_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "index" AS "index",
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_time AS txn_time,
  item_code AS item_code,
  CAST("qty_sold(kg)" AS REAL) AS "qty_sold(kg)",
  CAST("unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS REAL) AS "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg",
  "sale/return" AS "sale/return",
  CAST("discount(%)" AS INTEGER) AS "discount(%)",
  day_of_week AS day_of_week
FROM veg_txn_df
WHERE item_code IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized projection of veg_txn_df converting numeric columns and exposing raw categorical fields for joins to veg_cat or wholesale prices. Use when analyzing item-level sales, quantities, and pricing. | Use for: total kg sold per item or category; average selling price and discount analysis; time-of-day or day-of-week patterns in vegetable sales

views.name: veg_wholesale_prices_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "index" AS "index",
  whsle_date AS whsle_date,
  item_code AS item_code,
  CAST("whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS REAL) AS "whsle_px_rmb-kg"
FROM veg_whsle_df
WHERE item_code IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical projection of veg_whsle_df with typed wholesale price and date preserved. Use to join to veg transaction lines by item_code and date for cost/profit analyses. | Use for: compare wholesale vs selling price by item and date; compute gross margin per kg for vegetables

views.name: veg_item_dimension
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.item_code AS item_code,
  c.item_name AS item_name,
  c.category_code AS category_code,
  c.category_name AS category_name,
  l."loss_rate_%" AS "loss_rate_%"
FROM veg_cat c
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df l
  ON c.item_code = l.item_code
views.description: Item-level dimension combining veg_cat and veg_loss_rate_df to provide item_name, category and loss rate in one relation. Use to enrich transaction or wholesale rows with descriptive attributes. | Use for: category-level aggregations of sales or loss-adjusted quantities; enrich transactions with item_name and loss_rate for reporting

views.name: shopping_cart_events_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id AS visit_id,
  e.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  e.page_id AS page_id,
  p.page_name AS page_name,
  p.product_category AS product_category,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  e.event_type AS event_type,
  i.event_name AS event_name,
  e.sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  e.event_time AS event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
  ON e.event_type = i.event_type
views.description: Event-level feed joining shopping_cart_events to page hierarchy and event identifier to produce human-friendly event rows. Preserves visit_id/cookie_id/page_id and identifiers for downstream sessionization. | Use for: session funnel analysis (page sequences, drop-off points); count events by page_name or event_name; join events to user cookie or campaign attribution

views.name: shopping_cart_user_cookie_map
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  start_date AS start_date
FROM shopping_cart_users
WHERE cookie_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Mapping of shopping_cart_users preserving user_id, cookie_id and start_date for joins to events. Use to attribute events/visits to user_id where cookie_id matches. | Use for: attribute events or visits to users; cohorting users by start_date

views.name: bitcoin_txn_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.txn_id AS txn_id,
  t.member_id AS member_id,
  m.first_name AS first_name,
  m.region AS region,
  t.ticker AS ticker,
  t.txn_date AS txn_date,
  t.txn_type AS txn_type,
  CAST(t.quantity AS REAL) AS quantity,
  CAST(t.percentage_fee AS REAL) AS percentage_fee,
  t.txn_time AS txn_time
FROM bitcoin_transactions t
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members m
  ON t.member_id = m.member_id
views.description: Bitcoin transactions joined to bitcoin_members to expose member attributes (first_name, region). Useful for member-level transaction summaries and region-level crypto activity. | Use for: member-level crypto volume or fees by region; link transactions to prices by date

views.name: bitcoin_price_daily
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS market_date,
  CAST(price AS REAL) AS price,
  CAST(open AS REAL) AS open,
  CAST(high AS REAL) AS high,
  CAST(low AS REAL) AS low,
  volume AS volume,
  change AS change
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE market_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical projection of bitcoin_prices with typed numeric columns preserved for price/time analyses and joins to transactions by market_date. | Use for: time series of bitcoin prices; join prices to bitcoin transactions by date to compute realized P&L

views.name: customer_transactions_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_type AS txn_type,
  CAST(txn_amount AS INTEGER) AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Projection of customer_transactions with typed txn_amount and preserved txn_type for customer-level behavioral analysis and joins to customer_nodes or customer_regions. | Use for: customer deposit/withdrawal totals over time; join customer transactions to nodes or regions

views.name: customer_nodes_current
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  region_id AS region_id,
  node_id AS node_id,
  start_date AS start_date,

FROM customer_nodes
views.description: Latest node assignment per customer (selects the row with the most recent end_date or start_date if end_date NULL). Use to attribute a customer to their current node/region for analysis. | Use for: determine current node/region for a customer (requires downstream latest-per-customer filtering); historical node membership queries

views.name: interest_metrics_monthly
views.body_sql:
SELECT

  _year AS _year,

  interest_id AS interest_id,

FROM interest_metrics
WHERE interest_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized view of interest_metrics preserving year/month identifiers and measures for trend analysis or join to interest_map. | Use for: trend of index_value or composition by interest; rank and percentile based filters across months

views.name: interest_map_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  interest_name AS interest_name,
  interest_summary AS interest_summary,
  created_at AS created_at,
  last_modified AS last_modified
FROM interest_map
views.description: Simple projection of interest_map to provide interest_name and summary for enrichment of interest metrics. | Use for: join interest_metrics to interest_map for descriptive labels; list available interests and metadata

views.name: customer_transactions_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(customer_transactions.txn_date) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal', 'withdraw') THEN -1 * customer_transactions.txn_amount
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) IN ('deposit', 'payment', 'credit') THEN customer_transactions.txn_amount
    ELSE customer_transactions.txn_amount
  END AS txn_amount_signed,
  customer_transactions.txn_type AS txn_type,
  rowid AS txn_id
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Canonicalized customer transaction rows with parsed txn_date (date only), a signed txn_amount where debit types (e.g., 'withdrawal','withdraw') are negative and deposit-like types are positive, and any unknown types treated as deposits. Keeps one row per original transaction.

views.name: customer_monthly_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  date(date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-month aggregates of transactions: total net change in that month and the month start/end dates. One row per customer per year/month representing all transactions within that calendar month.

views.name: global_month_calendar
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start) AS month_start_date,
  -- month_end is last day of the month: take first day of next month minus one day
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  CAST((strftime('%Y', month_start) || printf('%02d', CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER))) AS INTEGER) AS month_seq
FROM (
  -- generate one row per month between min and max txn_date in customer_transactions
  SELECT date(
           strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn),
           '+' || (n) || ' months'
         ) AS month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT
      MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn,
      MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) bounds,
  -- generate sequence numbers from 0 up to number of months difference
  (SELECT
     (SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
      FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
     ) AS month_diff
  ),
  -- numbers table using recursive CTE emulation via cross join of small constants
  (SELECT (a.i + b.i*10) AS n
   FROM (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) a,
        (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) b
  )
  WHERE n <= (
    SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
    FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
  )
)
views.description: Continuous list of calendar months (year, month) covering the full date range from the earliest transaction date in the table to the latest transaction date, with month_start_date and month_end_date for each month. This is a global months scaffold used to ensure continuity for all customers.

views.name: customer_monthly_balance_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ca.customer_id,
  gc.year,
  gc.month,
  gc.month_start_date,
  gc.month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance is cumulative sum of monthly_net_amount up to and including this month
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        -- first month_seq for this customer
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      )
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance this month - closing_balance previous month
  COALESCE((
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
    -
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= (gc.month_seq - 1)
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
  ), 0) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance is alias of closing_balance
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      )
  ), 0) AS cumulative_balance
FROM
  (
    -- distinct customers that have aggregates
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_aggregates
  ) AS ca
CROSS JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc
-- restrict calendar to between each customer's first and last month by ensuring month_seq within customer's range
WHERE gc.month_seq BETWEEN
  (
    SELECT MIN(gc_min.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_min
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_min
      ON agg_min.year = gc_min.year AND agg_min.month = gc_min.month
    WHERE agg_min.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
  AND
  (
    SELECT MAX(gc_max.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_max
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_max
      ON agg_max.year = gc_max.year AND agg_max.month = gc_max.month
    WHERE agg_max.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
views.description: For every customer and every calendar month in the global month calendar between that customer's first and last month (inclusive), produce rows with closing_balance at month_end (running cumulative sum of monthly_net_amounts up to that month), monthly_change (difference vs prior month) and cumulative_balance (alias of closing_balance). Includes months with no transactions by carrying forward previous closing balance.

views.name: distinct_customers_from_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: All distinct customer_id values that appear in the customer_transactions table (the universe of customers for downstream computations). This is a simple row subset/cohort extraction.

views.name: customer_transactions_2020_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  substr(txn_date,1,7) AS year_month,
  txn_type,
  COALESCE(txn_amount, 0) AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01' AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
views.description: All customer_transactions rows constrained to the year 2020 with normalized/cleaned columns: transaction date, year-month string in 'YYYY-MM' format, txn_type preserved, and txn_amount cast with NULLs treated as zero.

views.name: customer_monthly_net_by_txn_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date,1,7) AS year_month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN IFNULL(txn_amount,0) ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN IFNULL(txn_amount,0) ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawals,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN IFNULL(txn_amount,0)
           WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -IFNULL(txn_amount,0)
           ELSE IFNULL(txn_amount,0) END) AS month_net
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, substr(txn_date,1,7)
views.description: For each customer_id and calendar month (year_month), compute aggregated sums of txn_amount partitioned by txn_type (separately sum deposits and withdrawals) and the net month transaction amounts per customer-month. NULL txn_amounts are treated as zero during aggregation.

views.name: customer_monthly_balance_including_zeros
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  printf('%04d-%02d', gc.year, gc.month) AS year_month,
  COALESCE(agg.monthly_net_amount, 0) AS month_end_balance
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
CROSS JOIN
  (SELECT year, month FROM global_month_calendar WHERE year = 2020) gc
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      printf('%04d-%02d', year, month) AS year_month,
      SUM(monthly_net_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates
    GROUP BY customer_id, year, month
  ) agg
  ON agg.customer_id = c.customer_id
  AND agg.year_month = printf('%04d-%02d', gc.year, gc.month)
views.description: All combinations of every distinct customer (from the universe of customers) with every calendar month present in 2020 (one row per customer_id and year_month), left-joined to the per-customer-month aggregated net amounts so that months without transactions produce month_end balance = 0. Produces the month-end balance per customer-month to be used for counting positive balances and computing averages.

views.name: clean_customer_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(txn_date))) AS txn_month_start,
  lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ABS(txn_amount)
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ABS(txn_amount)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_amount_signed
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
views.description: Canonicalize and filter customer_transactions to rows for valid transaction types, parse txn_date to a date, normalize txn_type to lower-case, and set txn_amount sign (deposits positive, withdrawals negative). Keeps one row per original transaction.

views.name: customer_monthly_net
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END
  ) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
views.description: Aggregate cleaned transactions to customer-month level using the month identifier as the first day of the month (YYYY-MM-01). Sum signed amounts to produce the net amount for that calendar month per customer and record the month identifier.

views.name: customer_monthly_closing_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cma.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cma.month_start AS month_start,
  -- numeric month ordering to identify prior calendar month relationships
  (CAST(strftime('%Y', cma.month_start) AS INTEGER) * 12 + CAST(strftime('%m', cma.month_start) AS INTEGER)) AS month_order,
  cma.monthly_net_amount AS monthly_net_amount,
  -- running sum (closing balance) over months per customer ordered by month_start
  SUM(cma.monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY cma.customer_id ORDER BY cma.month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_monthly_net cma
views.description: For each customer, order months chronologically and compute the cumulative closing balance at the end of each month (running sum of monthly_net_amount). Also include the numeric month ordering to identify prior calendar month relationships.

views.name: customer_latest_month_growth_rate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- latest month start for customer
  lm.month_start_date AS latest_month_start,
  lm.closing_balance AS latest_closing_balance,
  -- prior month info
  pm.month_start_date AS prior_month_start,
  COALESCE(pm.closing_balance, 0) AS prior_closing_balance,
  -- growth rate: if prior_closing_balance = 0 then current * 100 else (current - prior)/ABS(prior)
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(pm.closing_balance, 0) = 0 THEN (lm.closing_balance) * 100.0
    ELSE (lm.closing_balance - pm.closing_balance) / ABS(pm.closing_balance)
  END AS growth_rate
FROM
  (
    -- compute each customer's latest month_start (by month_end date)
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MAX(month_start_date) AS latest_month_start
    FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) latest
  JOIN customer_monthly_balance_rows lm
    ON lm.customer_id = latest.customer_id
    AND lm.month_start_date = latest.latest_month_start
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balance_rows pm
    ON pm.customer_id = lm.customer_id
    AND pm.month_start_date =
      (
        -- prior calendar month start: find the max month_start_date < latest month_start_date for same customer
        SELECT MAX(month_start_date)
        FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows sub
        WHERE sub.customer_id = lm.customer_id
          AND sub.month_start_date < lm.month_start_date
      )
  JOIN
    (
      -- ensure one row per customer even if no months exist (preserve joinability to customer list)
      SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows
    ) mb
    ON mb.customer_id = lm.customer_id
views.description: For each customer, identify the most recent month (latest month_start with any txn) and compute that month's growth rate compared to the prior calendar month's closing balance. If no prior month exists, prior closing balance = 0. If prior closing balance = 0, growth_rate = current_closing_balance * 100, else growth_rate = (current_closing_balance - prior_closing_balance)/ABS(prior_closing_balance).

views.name: customer_transactions_normalized_25
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal', 'withdraw', 'withdrawal_fee', 'fee') THEN -txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit', 'credit', 'refund') THEN txn_amount
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: One row per raw customer transaction with canonicalized date and signed txn_amount. Ensures txn_date is cast to ISO date and txn_amount reflects sign (if txn_type encodes direction, convert to signed amount).

views.name: calendar_months_from_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) AS month,
  date(substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01') AS month_first_day
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY month
views.description: One row per calendar month present in the transactions data. Derives the month identifier (YYYY-MM) and the month's first_day (date). Includes all months observed so they can be used as targets and baselines.

views.name: customer_cumulative_balance_as_of_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  d.as_of_date AS as_of_date,
  COALESCE(SUM(prev.txn_amount), 0) AS cumulative_balance
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) ct
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT txn_date AS as_of_date FROM customer_transactions
  ) d
LEFT JOIN
  customer_transactions prev
  ON prev.customer_id = ct.customer_id
  AND prev.txn_date < d.as_of_date
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  d.as_of_date
views.description: Per customer and reference date, compute the cumulative sum of txn_amount for all transactions strictly before that reference date. This produces one row per customer per reference date representing balance as-of that date.

views.name: customer_nonnegative_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  cb.as_of_date,
  CASE
    WHEN cb.cumulative_balance < 0 THEN 0
    ELSE cb.cumulative_balance
  END AS nonnegative_balance
FROM customer_cumulative_balance_as_of_date cb
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
) c ON c.customer_id = cb.customer_id
views.description: Normalize per-customer balances by replacing any negative cumulative_balance with zero. One row per customer per as_of_date with nonnegative_balance.

views.name: customer_txn_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  row_number() OVER (ORDER BY txn_date, rowid) AS txn_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date, ' ') + 1) AS txn_time,
  lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
  txn_amount,
  CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
       ELSE -txn_amount END AS signed_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Canonicalized customer transactions: normalize txn_date to DATE, canonicalize txn_type casing, and assign signed_txn_amount where deposits are positive and all other txn types are negative. Preserve original txn ordering columns.

views.name: customer_daily_running_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id,
  date(cal.day) AS calendar_date,
  COALESCE(
    (
      SELECT SUM(c2.signed_txn_amount)
      FROM customer_txn_canonical c2
      WHERE c2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
        AND date(c2.txn_date) <= cal.day
    ),
    0
  ) AS daily_running_balance
FROM
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_txn_canonical
  ) ct
CROSS JOIN
  (
    -- generate calendar spanning from earliest to latest txn_date across customers
    SELECT date(min_date, '+' || n || ' days') AS day
    FROM (
      SELECT date(min(txn_date)) AS min_date, date(max(txn_date)) AS max_date
      FROM customer_txn_canonical
    ), (
      SELECT 0 AS n
      UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
      UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
      UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14
      UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
      UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24
      UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
      UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34
      UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
      UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44
      UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
      UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54
      UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
      UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64
      UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
      UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74
      UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
      UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84
      UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
      UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94
      UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
    )
    WHERE date(min_date, '+' || n || ' days') <= (SELECT date(max(txn_date)) FROM customer_txn_canonical)
  ) cal
views.description: Per customer, one row per calendar date with the running account balance as of that date. Fill forward balances across dates with no transactions (carry last known running balance). The running balance is computed by ordering transactions by date (and time if present) and cumulatively summing signed_txn_amount.

views.name: customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.calendar_date,
  AVG(d2.daily_running_balance) AS rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM customer_daily_running_balance d
JOIN customer_daily_running_balance d2
  ON d.customer_id = d2.customer_id
  AND d2.calendar_date BETWEEN date(d.calendar_date, '-29 days') AND d.calendar_date
-- ensure at least 30 calendar days of history up to calendar_date for that customer
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM customer_daily_running_balance firstd
  WHERE firstd.customer_id = d.customer_id
    AND date(firstd.calendar_date) <= date(d.calendar_date, '-29 days')
)
GROUP BY
  d.customer_id,
  d.calendar_date
views.description: Per customer and calendar_date, the 30-day rolling average of daily_running_balance using the current date and preceding 29 calendar days. Only include rows where the customer has at least 30 days of daily balance history up to that date (i.e., at least 30 calendar days since their first txn_date). Do not clamp negatives here; keep numeric rolling_avg_balance.

views.name: customer_monthly_max_30day_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(r.calendar_date,1,7) AS month,
  MAX(CASE WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE r.rolling_30d_avg_balance END) AS monthly_max_30day_avg_clamped
FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance r
JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(substr(calendar_date,1,7)) AS baseline_month
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id
) b ON r.customer_id = b.customer_id
WHERE substr(r.calendar_date,1,7) <> b.baseline_month
GROUP BY r.customer_id, substr(r.calendar_date,1,7)
views.description: Per customer and calendar month (YYYY-MM), compute the maximum of the 30-day rolling averages within that month after replacing any negative rolling averages with zero. Exclude the customer's baseline month (the month of their first transaction) from output.
